lesson.1.drill.0: Get comfortable: guitar on your leg, fretting thumb behind the neck
lesson.1.drill.1: Pluck open strings low to high and say each name
lesson.1.drill.2: Hold each open string about two seconds — if it dies early, pluck again softer and cleaner
lesson.1.goal.0: Sit so your shoulders can stay loose
lesson.1.goal.1: Name the open strings low to high: E A D G B E
lesson.1.goal.2: Get all six open strings to ring without buzz
lesson.1.mastery: Name and pluck all six open strings in order without peeking at the headstock.
lesson.1.theory: Thick to thin, standard tuning is E A D G B E. Saying the names out loud while you pluck trains your ear for free.
lesson.1.title: Meet the Guitar — First Clean Sounds
lesson.10.drill.0: Freeze A and audit string by string — stop and fix buzz before you add speed
lesson.10.drill.1: A–D–E–A twice at a walking pace — mute the open strings you do not want
lesson.10.drill.2: Toggle A vs Am on a steady beat — hear major brighten and minor soften
lesson.10.goal.2: Toggle A vs Am so you hear the third
lesson.10.mastery: Play two full A–D–E loops with steady time. Do it twice so it was not a lucky fluke.
lesson.10.theory: A major is A C# E. It’s a gateway to blues and rock in A. Often one finger is all that separates major from minor color.
lesson.10.title: A Major — A–D–E Starter Set
lesson.11.drill.0: Pulse the fret-5 root on beat 1 for 30 seconds before leaving it
lesson.11.drill.1: Ascend box 1, rest one full bar, then descend — keep the foot tapping
lesson.11.drill.2: Three-note solo rule: pick any three box notes and make rhythm do the work for 60 seconds
lesson.11.goal.0: Find the A root for box 1 on the low E string at fret 5
lesson.11.goal.1: Walk the box up and down slowly with a pulse
lesson.11.goal.2: Improvise for one minute using only three notes from the box
lesson.11.mastery: Play box 1 up and down in time at ~60 BPM and land on the A root.
lesson.11.theory: After a week of chords, five notes are enough for first lead. A minor pentatonic is A C D E G. Box 1 (root on low-E fret 5) is the common rock/blues map — fewer notes means more room for rhythm and space, which is how solos start sounding like music.
lesson.11.title: Minor Pentatonic Box 1 — First Lead Map
lesson.12.drill.0: Learn phrase 1 only until you can play it twice without stopping
lesson.12.drill.1: Call-and-response: sing the next phrase, then play it at the same speed
lesson.12.drill.2: One slow clean pass through the whole Twinkle melody with a steady foot pulse
lesson.12.goal.0: Learn the melody in short phrases
lesson.12.goal.1: Sing a phrase, then play it
lesson.12.mastery: Play Twinkle phrase-by-phrase with a steady pulse and no rushing.
lesson.12.theory: Melodies train ear and timing faster than empty shapes. Treat each phrase like a sentence — breathe between them. Singing a line before you play it is one of the fastest ways to stop guessing on the neck.
lesson.12.title: First Melody — Twinkle in Open Position
lesson.13.drill.0: Spider on B and high E only — even volume, no flying fingers
lesson.13.drill.1: Add the G string only when the first two notes are already even
lesson.13.drill.2: Stop at the first real tension; shake out ten seconds
lesson.13.goal.0: Run 1-2-3-4 moving from string to string
lesson.13.goal.2: Choose a speed where the notes stay even
lesson.13.mastery: Play a calm two-string spider for 60 seconds with even volume.
lesson.13.theory: Independence is coordination, not strength. Slow spiders wire clean fretting for every chord you’ll learn later.
lesson.13.title: Finger Independence — Spider Across Strings
lesson.14.drill.0: Build E5 (open low E + A fret 2), G5 (low E fret 3 + A fret 5), then A5 (low E fret 5 + A fret 7); play only those two strings
lesson.14.drill.1: Palm-mute eighth notes on one power chord for 60 seconds with a foot pulse
lesson.14.drill.2: Four-bar riff: two bars on frets 3/5, two bars on frets 5/7, then reverse — keep unused strings quiet
lesson.14.goal.0: Fret a root + fifth power shape on the low strings
lesson.14.goal.1: Mute the strings you are not using
lesson.14.goal.2: Move the same grip up the neck in time
lesson.14.mastery: Play a four-bar power-chord riff twice with clear muting and steady time.
lesson.14.theory: A power chord is root + fifth (often with the octave). No third means it is neither major nor minor — that is why it moves so easily and sounds tough. Learn the grip once; the neck becomes a map of roots.
lesson.14.title: Power Chords Intro — Two-Finger Rock
lesson.15.drill.0: G→C only for two minutes at ~50 BPM — fretting hand arrives early, strum arm stays lazy
lesson.15.drill.1: C→D only for two minutes — plant the D triangle before you leave C
lesson.15.drill.2: Full G–C–D–G loop; watch one change and shrink the biggest motion you see
lesson.15.goal.1: Park shared fingers when you can
lesson.15.mastery: Make eight G–C–D changes where each landing is clean on beat 1.
lesson.15.theory: Economy of motion beats raw finger speed. Watch the shortest path between G, C, and D — shared fingers and small lifts are the real beginner skill, not slamming shapes from scratch every time.
lesson.15.title: Switching Lab — Shrink the Motion
lesson.16.drill.0: Play the motif only, four times, before expanding
lesson.16.drill.1: Motif | C chord | motif | G chord — name what you hear on the clean reps
lesson.16.drill.2: Soft question, fuller answer — light dynamics — shoulders down, thumb behind the neck
lesson.16.goal.1: Alternate the motif with a C or G chord
lesson.16.mastery: Play the Ode motif twice and answer each time with a clean open chord.
lesson.16.theory: A single-note theme over open chords builds the lead-and-rhythm brain without drowning you in theory.
lesson.16.title: Ode to Joy Motif — Melody Meets Chords
lesson.17.drill.0: Foot-only quarters for 30 seconds — stop and fix buzz before you add speed
lesson.17.drill.1: Muted groove for one minute — right hand stays in time, left hand mutes
lesson.17.drill.2: G–C–D with the foot locked; restart the bar if the foot rushes
lesson.17.goal.0: Foot taps quarters the whole drill
lesson.17.goal.1: Strum arm keeps moving even when you miss a change
lesson.17.goal.2: Prefer pocket at 70 BPM over chaos at 100
lesson.17.mastery: Two minutes of chord changes where your foot never stops the pulse.
lesson.17.theory: Listeners feel time before they notice fancy chords. Pocket means your notes agree with the pulse. Keep shoulders soft; clean and slow today becomes easy later.
lesson.17.title: Rhythm Guitar Feel — Pocket Over Speed
lesson.18.drill.0: Pluck Dm string-by-string and fix dead notes — stop and fix buzz before you add speed
lesson.18.drill.1: D | Dm | D | Dm — feel the one-finger shift, no rush between colors
lesson.18.drill.2: Loop Dm–C–G–G four times with even strums — shoulders down, thumb behind the neck
lesson.18.goal.1: Toggle D major vs D minor
lesson.18.goal.2: Play a tiny sad loop Dm–C–G
lesson.18.mastery: Show D vs Dm clearly, then play one clean Dm–C–G loop.
lesson.18.theory: Minor lowers the third — F instead of F# in D. Your ear learns faster when you A/B the colors on purpose.
lesson.18.title: D Minor & Mood — Major vs Minor Ears
lesson.19.drill.0: Freeze G7 for a bar, then resolve to C like a door closing
lesson.19.drill.1: Freeze D7 for a bar, then resolve to G — hear the pull home
lesson.19.drill.2: Loop G–G7–C four times and listen for the magnet
lesson.19.goal.1: Feel how V7 pulls toward I
lesson.19.mastery: Play two clear V7→I resolutions: G7→C and D7→G. Do it twice so it was not a lucky fluke.
lesson.19.theory: A dominant 7th (1–3–5–b7) creates tension that wants the home chord. Folk and blues live on that pull.
lesson.19.title: Seventh Color — G7 and D7 as Magnets
lesson.2.drill.0: Slow spider 1-2-3-4 on the high E around 50 BPM — stop and fix buzz before you add speed
lesson.2.drill.1: Buzz-then-add: ease off until it buzzes, then add a hair of pressure
lesson.2.drill.2: Quick mirror check — curved knuckles, wrist not collapsed
lesson.2.goal.0: Fret with fingertips, right behind the metal fret
lesson.2.goal.1: Use the lightest press that still sounds clean
lesson.2.goal.2: Play frets 1–4 on the high E evenly
lesson.2.mastery: Play frets 1–4 on the high E evenly at 60 BPM with clear tone.
lesson.2.theory: One fret is one half-step. Press just behind the fret wire — middle of the box makes you squeeze harder for a worse sound.
lesson.2.title: Fretting Hand — Just Enough Pressure
lesson.20.drill.0: Thumb on open A only for one minute — stop and fix buzz before you add speed
lesson.20.drill.1: Add index on the B string on the &s — name what you hear on the clean reps
lesson.20.drill.2: Run the pattern over an Am shape for 8 bars — shoulders down, thumb behind the neck
lesson.20.goal.1: Index answers on a higher string
lesson.20.mastery: Play 8 bars of thumb-bass + index answer without rushing.
lesson.20.theory: Travis-style seeds start with thumb independence. A steady bass makes sparse treble sound pro. Keep shoulders soft; clean and slow today becomes easy later.
lesson.20.title: Simple Fingerstyle Seed — Thumb + i
lesson.21.drill.0: One-finger barre chirps, ten times — stop and fix buzz before you add speed
lesson.21.drill.1: Fmaj7 (easy version) as an alternate win — name what you hear on the clean reps
lesson.21.drill.2: Shake out both hands every 30 seconds before tension sneaks in
lesson.21.goal.0: Barre high E and B at fret 1 lightly
lesson.21.goal.1: Add more of the F shape only if it stays painless
lesson.21.mastery: Sound two clean treble strings under a light fret-1 barre ten times.
lesson.21.theory: Full F barre is a milestone, not a day-one law. Mini shapes and patience beat forced pain. Keep shoulders soft; clean and slow today becomes easy later.
lesson.21.title: Barre Preview — One-Finger Mini F
lesson.22.drill.0: Hum a note, hunt it on the neck, check — five calm rounds
lesson.22.drill.1: Change the starting pitch once and hunt the new note cleanly
lesson.22.drill.2: Don’t write it down — trust your ears — shoulders down, thumb behind the neck
lesson.22.goal.1: Find it starting on open B or high E
lesson.22.goal.2: Repeat until fingers match your voice
lesson.22.mastery: Match a hummed 3-note idea on the guitar twice in a row.
lesson.22.theory: Voice to fret is the shortest path to owning music. Wrong notes are clues, not crimes. Keep shoulders soft; clean and slow today becomes easy later.
lesson.22.title: Ear Starter — Find Melodies You Hum
lesson.23.drill.0: G–C–D at whisper volume with locked time — stop and fix buzz before you add speed
lesson.23.drill.1: Same progression at conversation level — name what you hear on the clean reps
lesson.23.drill.2: Eight soft bars, then eight fuller bars — shoulders down, thumb behind the neck
lesson.23.goal.0: Play the same progression at two volumes
lesson.23.goal.1: Change volume with the right hand, not a death grip
lesson.23.mastery: Play 16 bars with a soft-to-louder lift someone else could notice.
lesson.23.theory: Expression is mostly right hand. Same chords, different story — instant “oh, that sounds like a song” upgrade.
lesson.23.title: Dynamics — Soft Verse, Bigger Chorus
lesson.24.drill.0: Palm-muted open low-E eighths near the bridge — stop and fix buzz before you add speed
lesson.24.drill.1: Chuck lightly on the &s between chord hits — groove, not noise
lesson.24.drill.2: Full stop rests for one bar in every four — shoulders down, thumb behind the neck
lesson.24.goal.1: Mute idle strings with the fretting hand
lesson.24.mastery: Play 8 bars where mutes and rings are obviously on purpose.
lesson.24.theory: Great rhythm guitar is half silence. Mutes turn strums into drums — practice the quiet as hard as the hit.
lesson.24.title: Mute Craft — Left and Right Hand Silence
lesson.25.drill.0: Build a cell on the high strings — stop and fix buzz before you add speed
lesson.25.drill.1: Cell | Em | cell | G — leave a breath before each chord so the cell stays clear
lesson.25.drill.2: Say the sketch’s name out loud — silly names welcome
lesson.25.goal.1: Answer it with Em or G
lesson.25.goal.2: Loop it as a tiny original
lesson.25.mastery: Perform your 4-bar sketch twice from memory. Do it twice so it was not a lucky fluke.
lesson.25.theory: Making something tiny of your own locks skills better than drills alone. Small songs beat perfect exercises.
lesson.25.title: Song Sketch — Combine Melody + Two Chords
lesson.26.drill.0: Chord hits on beat 1 only for 8 bars — silence is part of the groove
lesson.26.drill.1: Hits on 1 and 3 for 8 bars; keep 2 and 4 empty on purpose
lesson.26.drill.2: Full quarters at 65 BPM with the click — every downstroke the same weight
lesson.26.goal.0: Play only on beat 1 of each bar for one minute
lesson.26.goal.1: Add more beats only when that feels solid
lesson.26.goal.2: Notice when you rush the easy bars
lesson.26.mastery: Stay with the click for 90 seconds of simple chord hits.
lesson.26.theory: A metronome tells the truth kindly. Landing late or early is just data for the next rep. Keep shoulders soft; clean and slow today becomes easy later.
lesson.26.title: Timing Honesty — Metronome as Friend
lesson.27.drill.0: Rank Em G C D A Am E from cleanest to messiest — stop and fix buzz before you add speed
lesson.27.drill.1: Ugly-chord gym for five minutes — freeze shapes, then release
lesson.27.drill.2: Progression with the ugly chord on every bar 2 — shoulders down, thumb behind the neck
lesson.27.goal.1: Give it five focused minutes alone
lesson.27.goal.2: Drop it back into a progression
lesson.27.mastery: Name your weakest chord and show ten cleaner frets of it than your usual rush job.
lesson.27.theory: Fixing the weak link beats replaying what already feels good. One rescue per session adds up fast. Keep shoulders soft; clean and slow today becomes easy later.
lesson.27.title: Review Web — Weakest Chord Rescue
lesson.28.drill.0: E7 for four bars, A7 for two, back again — stop and fix buzz before you add speed
lesson.28.drill.1: Long-short shuffle strum attempt — name what you hear on the clean reps
lesson.28.drill.2: Smile — feel over perfection today — shoulders down, thumb behind the neck
lesson.28.mastery: Play a slow E7/A7 groove that feels like one full blues chorus.
lesson.28.theory: Dominant chords plus a long-short shuffle feel = instant blues flavor, even before a full 12-bar form.
lesson.28.title: Blues Tease — E7 A7 Shuffle Feel
lesson.29.drill.0: Run a quick posture checklist: thumb, wrist, shoulders, breath
lesson.29.drill.1: Play four minutes, break thirty seconds, repeat — name what you hear on the clean reps
lesson.29.drill.2: Note any hand hotspots in your phone so you do not ignore pain
lesson.29.goal.0: Check thumb and wrist for strain signs
lesson.29.goal.1: Take a 30-second break every five minutes
lesson.29.goal.2: Fix strap or seat before you push hard
lesson.29.mastery: Finish today’s playing without pushing through sharp pain.
lesson.29.theory: There’s no badge for pain. The only technique that reaches day 365 is the one you can still do next week.
lesson.29.title: Comfort Setup — Pain Flags and Breaks
lesson.3.drill.0: Build Em, count to four, release — do that ten times
lesson.3.drill.1: Down-strums on beats 1 and 3 only — name what you hear on the clean reps
lesson.3.drill.2: String audit: pluck each string alone and fix anything dead
lesson.3.goal.0: Build open Em with two fingers
lesson.3.goal.1: Strum all six strings on the beat
lesson.3.goal.2: Lift Em off and put it back ten times cleanly
lesson.3.mastery: Hold Em for eight steady down-strums with every string ringing.
lesson.3.theory: E minor is the notes E G B. Open Em: middle finger on A string fret 2, ring on D string fret 2. Easiest full-sounding chord — we start here on purpose.
lesson.3.title: First Chord Win — E Minor
lesson.30.drill.0: Jot a three-minute order on paper — stop and fix buzz before you add speed
lesson.30.drill.1: Full run with no stops — restart only after the end
lesson.30.drill.2: Second run with soft and loud sections — shoulders down, thumb behind the neck
lesson.30.goal.0: Medley: a progression, a tiny melody, a groove
lesson.30.goal.2: End on a held final chord
lesson.30.mastery: Deliver about three minutes using at least three chords and one melodic idea.
lesson.30.theory: Performance is a skill: start, keep going, recover, end. Today proves you can transfer the month — not recite trivia.
lesson.30.title: Basics Capstone — 3-Minute Campfire Set
lesson.31.drill.0: Pick your two easiest open chords and change only on beat 1 for two minutes
lesson.31.drill.1: Same pair with a metronome under 70 BPM — if buzz appears, slow down again
lesson.31.drill.2: Record 30 seconds; listen once for timing, once for muted strings
lesson.31.goal.0: Name what “clean change” means for you today
lesson.31.goal.1: Keep G, C, D, and Em in the rotation without panic speed
lesson.31.goal.2: Leave with one pair of chords that improved
lesson.31.mastery: Two minutes of one chord pair where most downbeats ring clean at a humble tempo.
lesson.31.theory: This phase is about changes that ring, not a bigger chord dictionary. Slow accurate reps beat fast sloppy ones. We keep working G, C, D, and Em — the campfire set — until switches feel boring in a good way.
lesson.31.title: Chord Phase Open — Clean Changes First
lesson.32.drill.0: Freeze G and strum eight even downstrokes — fix buzz before you move
lesson.32.drill.1: G→C in half notes ×16 — left hand early, right hand lazy and steady
lesson.32.drill.2: Four-bar groove using only G and C; smile if it is slow and clean
lesson.32.goal.2: Keep the right hand pulsing through the switch
lesson.32.mastery: Sixteen controlled G→C changes with clear downbeats.
lesson.32.theory: Shared notes and a short path make G–C a high-ROI first highway. Practice the change as its own song: two chords, honest time, fretting hand arrives early, strum arm never freezes.
lesson.32.title: G–C Highway — Change Lab
lesson.33.drill.0: Freeze C and strum eight even downstrokes — fix buzz before you move
lesson.33.drill.1: C→D in half notes ×16 — left hand early, right hand lazy and steady
lesson.33.drill.2: Four-bar groove using only C and D; smile if it is slow and clean
lesson.33.goal.2: Keep the right hand pulsing through the switch
lesson.33.mastery: Sixteen controlled C→D changes with clear downbeats.
lesson.33.theory: C to D is a shape jump — plant D’s triangle early so beat 1 is not a surprise. Practice the change as its own song: two chords, honest time, fretting hand arrives early, strum arm never freezes.
lesson.33.title: C–D Highway — Change Lab
lesson.34.drill.0: Freeze D and strum eight even downstrokes — fix buzz before you move
lesson.34.drill.1: D→Em in half notes ×16 — left hand early, right hand lazy and steady
lesson.34.drill.2: Four-bar groove using only D and Em; smile if it is slow and clean
lesson.34.goal.2: Keep the right hand pulsing through the switch
lesson.34.mastery: Sixteen controlled D→Em changes with clear downbeats.
lesson.34.theory: D to Em flips mood; keep the right hand boring so the left hand can be accurate. Practice the change as its own song: two chords, honest time, fretting hand arrives early, strum arm never freezes.
lesson.34.title: D–Em Highway — Change Lab
lesson.35.drill.0: Freeze Em and strum eight even downstrokes — fix buzz before you move
lesson.35.drill.1: Em→Am in half notes ×16 — left hand early, right hand lazy and steady
lesson.35.drill.2: Four-bar groove using only Em and Am; smile if it is slow and clean
lesson.35.goal.2: Keep the right hand pulsing through the switch
lesson.35.mastery: Sixteen controlled Em→Am changes with clear downbeats.
lesson.35.theory: Em–Am are kin shapes — notice what can stay close to the string. Practice the change as its own song: two chords, honest time, fretting hand arrives early, strum arm never freezes.
lesson.35.title: Em–Am Highway — Change Lab
lesson.36.drill.0: Freeze Am and strum eight even downstrokes — fix buzz before you move
lesson.36.drill.1: Am→E in half notes ×16 — left hand early, right hand lazy and steady
lesson.36.drill.2: Four-bar groove using only Am and E; smile if it is slow and clean
lesson.36.goal.2: Keep the right hand pulsing through the switch
lesson.36.mastery: Sixteen controlled Am→E changes with clear downbeats.
lesson.36.theory: Am to E is drama in two grips; leave a hair of air if you need it, but keep the pulse. Practice the change as its own song: two chords, honest time, fretting hand arrives early, strum arm never freezes.
lesson.36.title: Am–E Highway — Change Lab
lesson.37.drill.0: Freeze E and strum eight even downstrokes — fix buzz before you move
lesson.37.drill.1: E→A in half notes ×16 — left hand early, right hand lazy and steady
lesson.37.drill.2: Four-bar groove using only E and A; smile if it is slow and clean
lesson.37.goal.2: Keep the right hand pulsing through the switch
lesson.37.mastery: Sixteen controlled E→A changes with clear downbeats.
lesson.37.theory: E–A is a rock gate on the neck — roots move, grip logic stays related. Practice the change as its own song: two chords, honest time, fretting hand arrives early, strum arm never freezes.
lesson.37.title: E–A Highway — Change Lab
lesson.38.drill.0: Freeze A and strum eight even downstrokes — fix buzz before you move
lesson.38.drill.1: A→D in half notes ×16 — left hand early, right hand lazy and steady
lesson.38.drill.2: Four-bar groove using only A and D; smile if it is slow and clean
lesson.38.goal.2: Keep the right hand pulsing through the switch
lesson.38.mastery: Sixteen controlled A→D changes with clear downbeats.
lesson.38.theory: A to D should feel like a bright lift; mute strings that do not belong in D. Practice the change as its own song: two chords, honest time, fretting hand arrives early, strum arm never freezes.
lesson.38.title: A–D Highway — Change Lab
lesson.39.drill.0: Freeze G and strum eight even downstrokes — fix buzz before you move
lesson.39.drill.1: G→Em in half notes ×16 — left hand early, right hand lazy and steady
lesson.39.drill.2: Four-bar groove using only G and Em; smile if it is slow and clean
lesson.39.goal.2: Keep the right hand pulsing through the switch
lesson.39.mastery: Sixteen controlled G→Em changes with clear downbeats.
lesson.39.theory: G–Em softens major to minor with a small story change — hear it, do not rush it. Practice the change as its own song: two chords, honest time, fretting hand arrives early, strum arm never freezes.
lesson.39.title: G–Em Highway — Change Lab
lesson.4.drill.0: Build G one finger at a time, then strum — fix buzz before speed
lesson.4.drill.1: Em | G at about 50 BPM, two bars each — name what you hear on the clean reps
lesson.4.drill.2: Keep the strum arm moving while your fretting hand switches
lesson.4.goal.1: Strum from the low E string
lesson.4.goal.2: Change Em to G in slow motion
lesson.4.mastery: Complete four clean Em→G changes in 30 seconds. Do it twice so it was not a lucky fluke.
lesson.4.theory: G major is G B D. Single shapes are nice; smooth changes are the real beginner skill. Keep shoulders soft; clean and slow today becomes easy later.
lesson.4.title: Second Chord — G Major + First Change
lesson.40.drill.0: Freeze C and strum eight even downstrokes — fix buzz before you move
lesson.40.drill.1: C→Am in half notes ×16 — left hand early, right hand lazy and steady
lesson.40.drill.2: Four-bar groove using only C and Am; smile if it is slow and clean
lesson.40.goal.2: Keep the right hand pulsing through the switch
lesson.40.mastery: Sixteen controlled C→Am changes with clear downbeats.
lesson.40.theory: C and Am are relatives — same neighborhood of notes, different home base. Practice the change as its own song: two chords, honest time, fretting hand arrives early, strum arm never freezes.
lesson.40.title: C–Am Highway — Change Lab
lesson.41.drill.0: Freeze G and strum eight even downstrokes — fix buzz before you move
lesson.41.drill.1: G→D in half notes ×16 — left hand early, right hand lazy and steady
lesson.41.drill.2: Four-bar groove using only G and D; smile if it is slow and clean
lesson.41.goal.2: Keep the right hand pulsing through the switch
lesson.41.mastery: Sixteen controlled G→D changes with clear downbeats.
lesson.41.theory: G–D is anthem fuel; big open strings still need quiet unused noise. Practice the change as its own song: two chords, honest time, fretting hand arrives early, strum arm never freezes.
lesson.41.title: G–D Highway — Change Lab
lesson.42.drill.0: Build Fmaj7 or mini-F; pluck string-by-string and fix mutes before strumming
lesson.42.drill.1: C→F-color changes for two minutes — hear the quality land before you leave
lesson.42.drill.2: Loop C–Am–Fmaj7–G at ballad tempo, four beats each chord
lesson.42.goal.0: Play an easy F-color grip that still functions as F in a progression
lesson.42.goal.1: String-audit until every intended string rings
lesson.42.goal.2: Use that F color inside C–Am–F–G without pain
lesson.42.mastery: Play one clean C–Am–F-color–G chorus that stays pain-free and musical.
lesson.42.theory: Full F barre is a strength project. Fmaj7 or a mini-F gives you F function in songs with less compression — successive approximation. Clarity on a few strings beats six muffled ones every time.
lesson.42.title: F Maj7 Gateway — Barre Without Tears
lesson.43.drill.0: Barre chirps on fret 1: light press, release before burn — about one minute total work
lesson.43.drill.1: Hold full F for four slow strums, shake out, repeat up to five times
lesson.43.drill.2: Song loop: full F for one bar, Fmaj7 for the next — still counts as F function
lesson.43.goal.0: Roll the barre finger for even light pressure
lesson.43.goal.1: Get melody strings (high E/B) clear before chasing all six
